title: Intermediate (MEC) with Integrated CA / CMA Foundation
tagline: MEC combines Intermediate studies with CA/CMA Foundation coaching, preparing students for accounting and finance careers.
eligibility: Pass in Class 10 (SSC / CBSE / ICSE or equivalent).
board: Board of Intermediate Education, Andhra Pradesh
overview: The MEC group (Mathematics, Economics, Commerce) is the natural launch-pad for a career in accounting and finance. In this integrated programme, students complete the regular two-year Intermediate course (Part I English, Part II Second Language, Part III Mathematics, Economics, Commerce) while receiving structured coaching for the CA Foundation or CMA Foundation examination, so that they are exam-ready by the time they finish Second Year.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: Pass in Class 10 (SSC / CBSE / ICSE or equivalent). Students register with ICAI (for CA) or ICMAI (for CMA) at the Foundation level after Class 10; they can appear for the Foundation examination only after appearing for / passing Class 12 (Intermediate).

items.text: Entry-level examination conducted by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI). It is held three times a year, in January, May/June and September.
Four papers of 100 marks each (total 400):
children: Paper 3: Quantitative Aptitude — Business Mathematics, Logical Reasoning and Statistics (objective, 2 hours)

items.text: Papers 3 and 4 are objective and carry negative marking (0.25 mark per wrong answer).
To pass: minimum 40% in each paper and 50% aggregate in one sitting. Verify the current passing rules at icai.org.
Students who later complete a commerce degree with 55% (or non-commerce with 60%) can enter CA Intermediate directly without the Foundation (Direct Entry route).
Six papers in two groups (each paper 100 marks):
children: Group I: Advanced Accounting; Corporate and Other Laws; Taxation (Income-tax Law and GST)
Group II: Cost and Management Accounting; Auditing and Ethics; Financial Management and Strategic Management

items.text: Students may attempt one group at a time or both together. Held three times a year.
Integrated Course on Information Technology and Soft Skills (ICITSS) must be completed before starting articleship.
Two years of practical training under a practising Chartered Accountant after passing both groups of CA Intermediate and completing ICITSS.
This is where students learn real audit, taxation and accounting work; a stipend is paid as per ICAI norms.
Six papers in two groups:
children: Group I: Financial Reporting; Advanced Financial Management; Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
Group II: Direct Tax Laws and International Taxation; Indirect Tax Laws; Integrated Business Solutions (multidisciplinary case study)

items.text: Applicable Self-Paced Online Modules and the Advanced ICITSS must also be cleared.
On passing CA Final and completing training, the student becomes a member of ICAI — a Chartered Accountant.
Conducted by the Institute of Cost Accountants of India (ICMAI). Examinations are held in June and December.

CMA Foundation: four papers — Fundamentals of Business Laws and Business Communication; Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting; Fundamentals of Business Mathematics and Statistics; Fundamentals of Business Economics and Management.
CMA Intermediate: eight papers in two groups.
CMA Final: eight papers in two groups, plus mandatory practical training (approximately 15 months) before qualifying.
CMA specialises in cost control, management accounting, costing systems and performance management — highly valued in manufacturing, infrastructure, PSUs and consulting.

sections.heading: Specializations
paragraphs: CA Foundation track / CMA Foundation track (students choose one; the Intermediate MEC syllabus is common to both).

items.text: Class 10 marks memo / pass certificate
Transfer certificate, study certificate, caste certificate (if applicable), Aadhaar, passport-size photographs
